newsitem.title: DUBAI: Foreigners safe in Iran - interior minister.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners safe in Iran - interior minister.

text.p: Foreigners are safe in Iran, the country's interior minister said on Sunday, dismissing a Berlin court's statements linking Tehran to political killings in Germany as politically motivated.

The minister, Ali Mohammad Besharati, told law enforcement commanders the protection of foreign nationals was given the highest priority in Iran, the Islamic Republic's official news agency IRNA reported.
He also expressed hope that the time would come when there would be no need for the presence of police at public places, the agency said.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Sunday the huge emotional reaction in Iran to the court's verdict was more than understandable.

The verdict 10 days ago prompted an official protest by Iran's leadership and unleashed a wave of protests in Tehran where thousands of people took to the streets and some tried to storm the German embassy.

Kinkel added that Bonn was taking seriously threats by a radical Islamic group in Iran to unleash suicide attacks against Germany. Tehran could be taken at its word that Germans would come to no harm, he said.
